findings.summary: Confirmation callback remains unbounded; outer node:test timeout does not unwind helper finally and leaves correction barrier unreleased.
findings.impact: The full-suite node:test timeout does not release the held correction if confirmation/record read stalls; the browser helper has the same callback gap and no outer timeout. No product clinical failure is demonstrated.

notes: Clinical backend API/schema/migration changes expressly authorized by frozen seven-issue contract.
Receipt and clinical record are atomic Serializable; bounded conflict retries; replay current scope and request hash; permissions remain at HTTP/tool action boundary.
Migration explicitly creates patient-cascading receipt table and composite actor/request key; migration must precede backend and frontend deployment.
Bounded server prescription authority keeps exact quantity, actor, multi-dose identity and one-off date/time; given/refused one-off read models retain day identity across band edits.
Europe/Rome explicit clock shared by due query and assistant; existing authorization/sample/window bounds preserved.
Client request nonce is actor/payload-digest scoped; no patient text/token persisted; session epoch guards preparation/response.
Complete patient-specific paging rejects foreign, duplicate, short or inconsistent snapshots, evicts rejected cache before explicit retry.
Strict false catalog status prevents automatic lookups; malformed/unreachable preserves prior behavior; public limiter unchanged.
Synthetic fixture cleanup bound to invocation-owned database marker, no dev DB, global lifecycle flock; pinned real font distribution, exact simulated token redaction only.
No added dependency, authentication bypass, external clinical inference, new debug logging or unrelated source changes observed.
